daas-irab:1-2.t: ﴿وَالضُّحى﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb of swearing; ﴿وَاللَّيْلِ﴾: conjoined to الضحى; ﴿إِذا﴾: an adverb of time; ﴿سَجى﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿ما﴾: negative; ﴿وَدَّعَكَ﴾: a past verb and its object; ﴿رَبُّكَ﴾: fāʿil (agent); the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position; ﴿وَما قَلى﴾: conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿وَلَلْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ), and الآخرة خير are a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿لَكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) خير; ﴿مِنَ الْأُولى﴾: attached to خير.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿وَلَسَوْفَ﴾: the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ) and سوف is a particle of the future; ﴿يُعْطِيكَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its object; ﴿رَبُّكَ﴾: fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿فَتَرْضى﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb whose agent is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ﴾: the hamza is a particle of interrogation and affirmation (taqrīr), and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam; the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿يَتِيماً﴾: second direct object; the clause is resumptive; ﴿فَآوى﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿وَوَجَدَكَ﴾: a past verb and its first object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿ضَالًّا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿فَهَدى﴾: conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿فَأَمَّا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition); ﴿أما﴾: a particle of condition and detailing; ﴿الْيَتِيمَ﴾: fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿فَلا تَقْهَرْ﴾: the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ (rābiṭa), and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:10-10.t: Conjoined to what precedes it, and the i'rab is clear.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿أَمَّا﴾: a particle of condition and detailing; ﴿بِنِعْمَةِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) حدث; ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿فَحَدِّثْ﴾: the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir).

farraa:1-2.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلضُّحَىٰ وَٱللَّيْلِ إِذَا سَجَىٰ﴾.
As for «الضحى», it is the whole of the daytime. ﴿وَٱللَّيْلِ إِذَا سَجَىٰ﴾: when it grows dark and becomes still in its length, just as you say: بحر ساج (a calm sea) and ليل ساج (a still night), when it is still, quiet and dark.

farraa:3-3.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَا وَدَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ وَمَا قَلَىٰ﴾.
It was revealed concerning the withholding of revelation from the Prophet ﷺ for fifteen [nights]. The idolaters said: Muhammad ﷺ has been forsaken by his Lord — or: the follower (al-tābiʿ) who used to be with him has come to hate him. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, revealed: ﴿مَا وَدَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿وَمَا قَلَىٰ﴾, meaning: وما قلاك (nor has He hated you). The kāf was dropped, just as one says: قد أعطيتك وأحسنتُ (I have given you and done well), meaning: أحسنت إليك (I have done well by you); one makes do with the first kāf rather than repeating the other. And [also] because the verse-endings are in yāʾ; so both [reasons] came together in it.

farraa:5-5.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضَىٰ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] it is: "ولسيعطيك [ربك فترضى]", and the meaning is the same, except that (سوف) became frequent in speech and its place became well known, so the fāʾ and the wāw were left out of it; when a word becomes frequent, that is sometimes done to it, as is said: أَيشٍ تقول (what are you saying?), and as is said: قم لا بَاك and قم لا بِشانئك, meaning: لا أبا لك and لا أبا لشانئك. I have heard a verse in which the fāʾ was elided from كيف; the poet said:
من طالبين لِبُعران لنا رفضت * كيلا يُحسون من بعراننا أثرا
(From people searching for camels of ours that had strayed off — how is it that they perceive no trace of our camels?)
He meant: كيف لا يحسون (how do they not perceive?). And this is like that.

farraa:6-6.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيماً فَآوَىٰ﴾.
He says: you were in the care of Abū Ṭālib, so He gave you a shelter and made you independent of him. It was not a wealth that came from abundance of property; rather Allah made him content with what He gave him.

farraa:7-7.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَوَجَدَكَ ضَآلاًّ فَهَدَىٰ﴾.
He means: [He found you] among a people gone astray, and He guided you. ﴿وَوَجدَكَ عائلاً﴾ (8): poor. I saw it in the muṣḥafs of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] as "عديما" (destitute), and the meaning is the same.

farraa:8-8.t: His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَغْنَىٰ﴾, and "فآوى": what is meant is (فأغناك) "so He enriched you" and (فآواك) "so He sheltered you". It went the way of dropping the kāf to match the verse-endings, and because the meaning is known.

farraa:9-9.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَمَّا ٱلْيَتِيمَ فَلاَ تَقْهَرْ﴾.
So that you take away his right because of his weakness. In the muṣḥaf of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] it is "فلا تكهر", and I heard it from a Bedouin of Banū Asad who recited it to me.

farraa:10-10.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَمَّا ٱلسَّآئِلَ فَلاَ تَنْهَرْ﴾.
The beggar at the [142/b] door. He says: either give to him, or turn him away with a gentle turning-away.

farraa:11-11.t:
His words, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿وَأَمَّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثْ﴾.
The Qur'an was Allah's greatest blessing upon him, so he used to recite it and speak of it, and of other than it among His blessings. [Translator's note: the source reads «ويغيره», which appears to be a corruption of «وبغيره» (and of other things); translated accordingly.]

zajjaj:1-2.t:
Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿والضُّحى﴾ ﴿واللَّيْلِ إذا سَجى﴾: this is an oath, and its answer is ﴿ما ودَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ وما قَلى﴾ [al-Ḍuḥā: 3]. ”اَلضُّحى“ is the daytime; and it was said: one of the hours of the day. And His saying ”إذا سَجى“ means "when it is still". The poet said:
يا حَبَّذا القَمْراءُ واللَّيْلُ السّاجْ ∗∗∗ وطُرُقٌ مِثْلُ مُلاءِ النَّسّاجْ
(How lovely the moonlit night and the still [al-sāj] night, and roads like the sheets of the weaver!)

zajjaj:3-3.t: And the meaning of ﴿ما ودَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ وما قَلى﴾ is: He has not cut off revelation from you, nor has He hated you. That is because revelation was delayed from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for fifteen days, and some people said: "Muhammad's companion has bidden him farewell and hated him." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down: ﴿ما ودَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ وما قَلى﴾. The meaning is "nor has He hated you", as He said: ﴿والذّاكِرِينَ اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا والذّاكِراتِ﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 35] ("and the men who remember Allah much and the women who remember"), the meaning being "and the women who remember Him".

zajjaj:6-6.t: And His saying: ﴿ألَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيمًا فَآوى﴾ ("did He not find you an orphan and give you shelter?"): the Prophet, peace be upon him, was in the care of his uncle Abū Ṭālib.

zajjaj:7-7.t: And His saying: ﴿وَوَجَدَكَ ضالا فَهَدى﴾ ("and He found you wandering and guided you"): its meaning — and Allah knows best — is that he did not know the Qur'an or the revealed laws, so Allah guided him to the Qur'an and the laws of Islam. The evidence for that is His saying: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ أوْحَيْنا إلَيْكَ رُوحًا مِن أمْرِنا ما كُنْتَ تَدْرِي ما الكِتابُ ولا الإيمانُ﴾ [al-Shūrā: 52] ("and thus We revealed to you a spirit of Our command; you did not know what the Book was, nor faith"). And some people said: he was upon the way of his people for forty years.

zajjaj:9-9.t: And His saying: ﴿فَأمّا اليَتِيمَ فَلا تَقْهَرْ﴾ ("so as for the orphan, do not oppress"): that is, do not overpower him regarding his property.

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿وَأمّا السّائِلَ فَلا تَنْهَرْ﴾ ("and as for the one who asks, do not repel"): that is, do not rebuff him; either give to him, or turn him away with a gentle turning away.

zajjaj:11-11.t: ﴿وَأمّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثْ﴾ ("and as for the favour of your Lord, proclaim it"): that is, convey what you have been sent with, and speak of the prophethood which Allah has given you, which is the greatest of favours.
